done_when: When the only failed required check is a review check that ran before the branch's latest commit, close re-runs that job once and waits for it.

known.title: Not done: Retry and wait for the only failed required review from an older commit
Functional: A current-head review can be mistaken for an old review
Test: Retry and wait for the only failed required review from an older commit
Functional: The repair rejects stale reviews whose runs report the base SHA

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - the review of commit A fails, the branch advances to B, and the workflow run reports the base SHA.
The repair still cannot find A's failed review. `_seen` requests statuses for the current head B (`src/forge/checks.py:840-842`), and [GitHub's combined-status endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/statuses#get-the-combined-status-for-a-specific-reference) returns statuses for that ref. The workflow posts A's result to A (`.github/workflows/forge.yml:180-195`), so it is absent from B's response; any status returned for B names B in its URL and is rejected by this guard. Close therefore never requests or waits for the stale review retry. The test at `tests/test_close_reruns_old_review.py:41` supplies A's status as a generic response to the request for B, masking the failure.
findings.title: Functional: The repair rejects stale reviews whose runs report the base SHA

why: A review check that failed before a CI fix stays failed until someone re-runs that job by hand, so close keeps reporting a failed check after the cause is fixed.
